headline: Book first.
Improve after.
coverSpec.title: The complete guide to US visa appointments in 2026, in the order the process actually happens
coverSpec.desc: Hold a confirmed appointment before doing anything else, because rescheduling moves a booking and cannot create one. Know how many changes your country allows, which differs by scheduling platform. Check every post your account offers, because intra-country gaps ran from about 15 to about 495 days in August 2026. Widen the range of dates you will accept, which is the biggest free lever. And use the free expedite request only where you meet the documented urgency criteria.

faq.q: What is the first thing to do about a US visa appointment?
faq.a: Complete the DS-160, pay the application fee, and take whatever interview date the system offers you, however distant. A confirmed appointment is the asset everything else depends on: you cannot reschedule what you do not hold, and you cannot make an expedite request without an existing booking. Waiting for a better date before booking is the most common self-inflicted delay in this process.

faq.q: How do I get an earlier US visa appointment?
faq.a: Four things, in order of how much difference they make. Check every consular post your scheduling account offers you, because gaps inside one country can run to hundreds of days. Widen the range of dates you will accept as far as your plans allow. Work the calendar for cancellations, which is where most earlier dates come from. And make the free expedited appointment request if you meet the documented urgency criteria.

faq.q: Which website do I use to book a US visa appointment?
faq.a: It depends on your country. India, Canada and many others use the AIS portal at ais.usvisa-info.com, while the UAE and others moved to usvisascheduling.com in 2025. Reach the correct one by following the link from your own embassy or consulate's website, both because it is the right platform for your country and because look-alike domains are a live problem in this market.

faq.q: How many times can I reschedule a US visa appointment?
faq.a: It is set per country by the scheduling platform, and the range is wide. India has allowed one change per application fee since 1 January 2025, while some countries allow three and some six. Your own account shows your remaining attempts, and that number overrides any article. Once they are exhausted, a new application fee is required before you can change anything.

faq.q: What does a US visa actually cost in 2026?
faq.a: For a B-1/B-2, the application fee is $185 and the $250 visa integrity fee is charged on issuance where a post is collecting it, so $435 per applicant. Petition-based categories pay $205 for the application fee. Some nationalities also owe a reciprocity fee. Nothing has a family rate, so a party of four is $1,740 before travel.

faq.q: Can I apply in a different country to get a faster interview?
faq.a: In almost all cases you should not. Since the State Department's guidance of 6 September 2025, updated on 10 October 2025, applicants are directed to schedule at the post in their country of nationality or legal residence, and those who apply elsewhere are warned they may find it more difficult to qualify. Fees are neither refunded nor transferred. The legitimate version of the same idea is a quieter post inside your own country.

faq.q: Is there any way to pay for a faster US visa interview?
faq.a: One, and it is available almost nowhere. The State Department's expedited appointment pilot lets B-1 and B-2 applicants pay $750 for an interview within ten business days, and as of 19 August 2026 it runs only at Mission Mexico and Mission Canada. It is per applicant, non-refundable, paid to the US government inside your own scheduling account, and scheduled to end on 31 December 2026.

faq.q: Does rescheduling hurt my visa application?
faq.a: No. Rescheduling is an administrative action in a scheduling system and has no bearing on how a consular officer assesses your eligibility. The only way it can hurt you is indirectly, by using up a limited number of attempts and leaving you unable to make a change you need later.

cta.heading: You now know everything we know. The rest is time
cta.body: That is the honest summary of this guide. There is no step we have held back, no method we have not described, and no access anybody has that you do not. What a service sells is somebody carrying the watching, the judgement about which openings are worth an attempt, and the persistence to keep at it for weeks. If you have the hours, do it yourself. If you do not, tell us your post, your current date and the widest range of dates you could accept, and we will tell you honestly whether it is worth paying us at all.
